matt: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-selector change I'm seeing a reproducible tail-latency regression on qwen2.5 8k in the dedicated pool. p50 ~22ms (no change) but p95 jumped from 120ms -> 210ms.

sara: ugh. same flavor as the 'kernel fallback' we saw last month? any traces/allocs? :thinking_face:

matt: dropping a minimal trace + chosen-kernel log. The runtime seems to pick autokernel-v2 for some requests instead of matmul_opt, and autokernel-v2 is doing a slow kv-copy path.

```
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] model=qwen2.5 variant=8k seq=2048 heads=32 kv_dim=64 chosen_kernel=autokernel-v2 reason="kv_head_mismatch"
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] latency_ms=218 p95_trace_id=tr-abc123
[2026-03-15T14:12:03Z] kernel_path=/runtimes/autokernel-v2/slow_kv_copy.cpp:line(482)
```

jun: interesting — kv_dim=64 vs head_dim=48? that would trigger the generic fallback in our kernel selector. Can you paste the exact model config the deployment is using (head count, kv dim, qk per head)?

matt: deployment metadata: `qwen2.5/8k@v3` (heads=32, head_dim=48, kv_dim=64). This mismatch only shows up on mixed-ling prompt inputs that hit tokenizer branch B. Single-language prompts pick the fast path.

anne: that smells like tokenizer-induced sequence chunking changing kv reshape. We've seen token-boundary splits expand seq len and end up with `kv_view` shape misaligned. Any repro with the multi-ling prompt?

matt: repro curl below (internal):

```
curl -s -X POST https://runtime.internal/redwood/infer \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"model":"qwen2.5/8k@v3","input":"zh: 今天的天气... en: what's the forecast" ,"stream":false}'
```

jun: run that with `RUNTIME_KERNEL_OVERRIDES=matmul_opt` set to see if we can force the fast kernel. If p95 drops that's confirmation it's selector logic. Also try `RUNTIME_TRACE=kvshape` to dump the reshape shape just before kernel pick.

matt: ran with overrides. p95 dropped back to ~125ms. Trace shows the reshape at decision point: `reshape_from=(32,64,64)` vs expected `reshape_from=(32,48,64)` — so kv head vs attn head dims swapped in one axis.

sara: so two orthogonal problems: 1) tokenizer branch produces a tokenization layout that mutates `head_dim` inference, 2) kernel selector logic isn't tolerant and prefers slower generic path. We should patch selector to accept certain mismatch patterns (e.g., allow kv_dim>head_dim with zero-copy adapter) and add a metric to count these fallbacks.

anne: +1. I can prototype a tolerant-match in the selector that tries a lightweight adapter shim: do a view+pad instead of full copy and then re-run autotuner. Will microbench. Also propose adding a small batch-sanity check in the batching heuristics to avoid mixing tokenization branches in the same minibatch — that would cut down on variance.

jun: for immediate mitigation, we can add a rollout that forces `kernel_preference: [matmul_opt, autokernel-v2]` for qwen2.5/8k on dedicated pools for accounts hitting >2 p95 regressions. I'll open a rollout canary.

ops-bot: deploy pipeline report — canary rollout started for runtime-config `kernel_preference_fallback_fix` at 2026-03-15T15:05:00Z.

matt: thanks. follow-ups: (1) anne to prototype adapter shim + PR, (2) jun to prepare a kernel-selector metric + canary, (3) sara to add tokenizer branch unit test that asserts kv/head dim invariants, (4) i'll collect 100 traces and attach to the perf dashboard.

sara: I'll add the unit test and a small tokenizer-normalization patch for CJK/latin switching — even a tiny normalization avoided the branch flip in local experiments.

matt: perfect. I'll file a short incident note and link the traces. Closing thread once PRs land. :thumbsup:
